analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop+InferenceHandler.swift (620–1556), the complete changed-range map, and the bounded patch. BASE shared-key setup and chunk encryption fail closed without sending plaintext (797–855), consistent with T-008/A-001/A-003. The surrounding pipeline partitions cache reuse by remote scope, emits cache evidence, accounts for delivered output on cancellation, and signs emitted response text (875–915, 1181–1304, 1361–1542); no supplied change establishes a regression in these controls (T-041, T-010, TB-007).
The visible deadline change replaces firstWithheldReasoningAt with firstWithheldOutputAt (HEAD 1147–1149). This broadens what stops the pre-content deadline, but the signal implementation and withheld-answer lifecycle are not supplied. Integration must verify that the timestamp represents genuine generated output, does not admit indefinite hidden buffering, and remains compatible with cancellation, partial billing and TTFT accounting (BASE 1214–1220, 1375–1388, 1494–1504). The later timestamp replacement is truncated in the patch and cannot be fully verified here.
New GLM5NextWiredLimitNotice.report calls receive raw errors at model load, stream startup and generation failure (HEAD 577, 1023, 1325). Review its implementation to confirm typed matching and privacy-safe diagnostics: BASE 1014–1029 and 1316–1321 deliberately sanitize errors that may contain prompt content. Missing implementation is an unverified contract, not evidence of disclosure. No independently supported new vulnerability is established within this source scope; these PR-specific contracts require reconciliation with the other source passes.
